newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-BENT WINS MEN'S 200 BACKSTROKE WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-BENT WINS MEN'S 200 BACKSTROKE WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Neisser Bent succeeded fellow Cuban Rodolfo Falcon as men's 200 metres backstroke world short-course champion on Friday, claiming victory with a powerful late surge.

Bent, Olympic 100 backstroke bronze medallist to Falcon's silver at the 1996 Atlanta Games, forced his way into contention late in the race after Russian veteran Vladimir Selkov had led through the first 150 metres.
Bent charged through on the last length to win in one minute 54.21 seconds.
China's Wang Wei, the fastest heat qualifier, took the silver in 1:54.82 and Selkov the bronze in 1:55.15.
Defending champion Falcon failed to make the final, finishing 19th overall in the morning's heats, more than five seconds behind top qualifier Wang.
